title: Why Resident Evil Isn't Called Biohazard
hook: In Japan the series has never once been called Resident Evil. The real name was blocked in America, so Capcom held a contest. Which name do you prefer?
script: Did you know Resident Evil has never been called Resident Evil in Japan? Over there, the series has always been Biohazard. That was the name Shinji Mikami and his team built the first game under in 1996, and it is still the name on every Japanese box today. The problem showed up when Capcom got ready to release the game in America. Biohazard was already taken. There was a hardcore punk band from New York called Biohazard, and Sega had released a game called Bio-Hazard Battle back in 1992, so Capcom's American office could not trademark it. Instead of paying lawyers, they ran a contest inside the company. Employees pitched replacement names, and the winner was Resident Evil, a nod to the fact that the whole first game takes place inside one mansion. Plenty of people inside Capcom thought the new name was cheesy. One of the marketing team's own members voted against it. It stuck anyway. Nearly thirty years and more than one hundred fifty million copies later, the biggest horror franchise in gaming still answers to two different names depending on which side of the ocean you are standing on. Follow for more gaming history.
